reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and, consistently, no redline or comment was proposed — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited text supports the conclusion: Section 7.4 (p0543) conditions a replacement subordination agreement on terms 'not less favorable in any material respect to SFJ' than the SVB subordination agreement — a lien-priority/refinancing benchmark against a specific existing document, not an obligation on PB to extend SFJ any better commercial terms granted to a third party, so it is not an MFN within the rule's detection guidance.

Section 7.5.5 (p0552) is a consent/negative-covenant right over Licensing Transactions tied to 'Material Impact'; it contains no match-or-pass-through mechanic, so it does not trigger the MFN rule (and any restrictive-covenant concern belongs to a different rule, avoiding double-flagging).

Rationale documents the negative search evidence ('most favored/favoured', 'no less favo(u)rable', 'at least as favorable', 'right of first refusal', 'third party offer'), which is adequate support for the preferred position of no MFN burdening our party; deterministic checks raised no issues.
